newsitem.title: USA: Cohen backs Ralston despite affair - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Cohen backs Ralston despite affair - spokesman.

text.p: Defense Secretary William Cohen supports Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston as a leading candidate to become the nation's top military officer despite Ralston's adulterous affair 14 years ago, Cohen's spokesman said on Thursday.

"He looked carefuly at the situation. He has not made any final decision, but he has not disqualified Ralston because of this," Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told Reuters as a major question arose over Ralston's qualification to become Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

Cohen himself told the Washington Post in an interview published on Thursday that he decided to retain Ralston, currently vice chairman of the joint chiefs, as a top candidate to succeed Army Gen. John Shalikashvili as chairman and that he had told members of Congress about the affair.

"This occurred a long time ago and the secretary feels that it is not a threat to good order and discipline" in the military, Bacon said on Thursday. "In a perfect world, there would be no separations or divorces."
Cohen told the paper the affair was about a year long and occurred while Ralstan and his first wife, Linda, were separated. The Ralstons reconciled for a time, but divorced in 1988.

The issue arose on the heels of a series of embarrassing incidents in which U.S. military officers have been removed from command or retired amid allegations of extra-marital affairs. The Army is also involved in a scandal involving rape and sexual harassment of female recruits by male drill sergeants.
